Visited Malgudi in Chembur recently and had a wonderful experience. The highlight of the meal was definitely the Mulbagal Onion Masala Dosa paired with the Cold Filter Kaapi—an amazing combination that I'll be coming back for.

We also tried the Ven Pongal Arancini, Ghee Podi Thatte Idli, and the Veg Malabar Curry with Malabar Parotta, all of which were flavorful and thoughtfully prepared. To finish, we had the Chocolate Pull Up Cake and Pal Payasam Kulfi, which were the perfect ending to the meal.

featured_reviews.name: Nikhil Kamath
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tried Shankar Mahadevan’s @malgudi.ind in Chembur during my recent Mumbai trip, a restaurant that’s become quite popular for its modern take on South Indian food. We started with the Anna Style Crispy Lotus Root, which had a tangy tamarind-heavy flavour and worked well as a snack. The much-hyped Mulbagal Dosa, though visually interesting with its parcel-like shape, tasted fairly ordinary. The Davangere Benne Podi Dosa followed a similar route, comforting but not very memorable beyond the podi and butter.

For the main course, we ordered Sanchi’s Vegetable Stew with Appam and Veg Malabar Curry with Malabar Parotta. The curry and parotta were satisfying, but the stew felt too watery and lacked the comforting richness you expect from a good appam-stew combination.

The real standout was the Filter Kaapi Panna Cotta. Smooth, creamy, and packed with coffee and jaggery flavour, it easily ended up being the best thing on the table.

featured_reviews.name: Mridula Bhat
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Malgudi – Shankar Mahadevan’s Resto Café Bar recently and it’s a refreshing take on South Indian cuisine.

What stands out is how they’ve retained the comfort of familiar flavours while introducing thoughtful, modern elements, especially in their coffee menu. The filter coffee variations are genuinely interesting.

The space itself has a warm, slightly nostalgic vibe.

Food quality was solid. Service was courteous.

We highly recommend Ghee Podi Thatthe Idli, Mulbagal Dosa, Mushroom Ghee Roast with Neer Dosa, Sri Lankan Tamil Curry with Idiyappam, Bisi Bele Bhaath and the soulful and delicious Sheera for dessert.

For drinks, we tried Mango Matcha Beery and Iced Kaapi (this had jaggery and ghee) and was delicious!

Overall, it’s a place worth visiting if you’re looking to experience South Indian food in a slightly elevated setting.

featured_reviews.name: Prachi Jaiswal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I usually go to Naveena for parotta and saru, but this time I decided to try this place. Unfortunately, the experience was quite disappointing.

We ordered parotta with saru, masala omelette, chicken biryani, and chicken 65.

The parotta was very rubbery and not enjoyable at all. They serve both chicken and mutton saru, but the taste was below average and the spice level was overwhelming. None of the food we ordered stood out in terms of taste.

The service was extremely slow. We ordered a masala omelette and chicken 65 to have with the parotta, but the omelette was completely forgotten, and the chicken 65 arrived only after we had finished the parotta and biryani.

The chicken biryani was dry, overly spicy, and loaded with too much whole masala (khada masala), which made it difficult to enjoy. The quantity of chicken 65 was also surprisingly small for the price.

Overall, we spent around ₹450 and felt it was not worth it. Between the below-average food, delayed service, and missed items, the experience was disappointing. I wouldn’t recommend this place based on my visit.

There is a long rectangular area with comfortable cozy sitting where staff always attends to your requests.

Note : One special table towards the end on the upper desk is best for dates or family dinner.  Its secluded & offers a private feel.

We ordered some starters like Tandoori Mushroom and Pahadi paneer,  the preparation along with the presentation was on the target (feel it through the pictures below) . They also offer some amazing breakfast items like various types of dosa, idli,  upma,  sheer,  medu vada,  pizza.  Juices here are good too.

Further,  you cannot afford to miss their Dal Khichadi and Palak khichadi, top notch perfection in taste with a perfect creamy blend of texture on both.

Try their various starters.  They dont disappoint.

Just one request Dear Sawali,  to justify your prices, pour in some more quantity.

customer_updates.text: We celebrated our friend Naresh Mehta Uncle's 80th birthday at Jeevan Boarding House with our biggest friend group, and it was a fantastic experience! featured_reviews.name: Moumita Roy
featured_reviews.review_text: Jeevan Boarding House is a hidden gem in Chembur for anyone looking for simple, homely food at an unbeatable price. For just ₹100, you get a complete meal starting from chutney and accompaniments all the way to a sweet dish. The food is fresh, tasty, and feels like a home-cooked meal. The service is quick, and the overall experience is great value for money. A must-visit if you’re looking for an affordable and satisfying meal.

featured_reviews.name: ashish kumar
featured_reviews.review_text: Good food. Enjoyed the fresh south indian dinner delicacies in banana leaf...cost for each only Rs 110/- and legendary outlet since 1962. I have travelled this place near Chembur Station more than 100 times but today found out through Google maps. Very nice experience.

featured_reviews.name: Saakshi Shinde
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had a special southindian lunch served by Jeevan Thali at our office in marol. The thali had absolutely amazing and truly satisfying. The meal was a perfect balance of flavors, textures, and authenticity. From the moment it was served, the aroma itself was enough to make me excited to dig in.

The thali included a variety of dishes like sambar, rasam, different vegetable curries, chutneys, all served with soft rice, crispy papad, and perfectly made chapatis, puranpoli, paysam. Each item had its own distinct taste—rich, flavorful, and well-seasoned without being too heavy.

What stood out the most was the freshness and authenticity of the preparation. The service was also warm and attentive, adding to the overall experience.

Overall, it was a wholesome, delicious, and fulfilling meal that truly represents the essence of South Indian cuisine. Definitely a must-try for anyone who loves traditional and flavorful food!

featured_reviews.name: PARIMAL BORKAR
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jeevan Boarding House is very near from Chembur East station not even minutes long Very huge free space outside the hotel. No seperate parking for hotel and if Park vehicle near hotel Road it cause towing as NO PARKING.
Food is amazing, staff is best, the way of serving is different that they use Banana leaf for every unlimited food by heart serving the staff. Pineapple Bhaji was different in taste, it tastes so good ki mood ban jaye. Rassam, curd, papad, two more Bhaji, sweet dish and everything fulfilled and make you satisfied.
So many varieties you need to visit and just taste it, menu changes day to day so please confirm the menu if you want to test pineapple Bhaji.
Suggestion is go by train if you live away from Chembur or use public utilities.
Because parking is on drawback.

featured_reviews.name: Akash Mande
featured_reviews.review_text: Jeevan Boarding House, Chembur is a classic South Indian restaurant with a legacy going back to 1962. The place serves simple, authentic South Indian food at very affordable prices. The taste is consistent, homely, and reminds you of old-school eateries that focus more on food than frills. Portions are satisfying, service is quick, and the atmosphere has a nostalgic charm. A must-visit for anyone who enjoys traditional South Indian meals without burning a hole in the pocket.

featured_reviews.name: Ajinkya Girmal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently shifted to Mumbai from Kolhapur. Being a bachelor, I’m always in search of homely food at an affordable rate, and after three months, I finally found Jeevan Boarding House simply divine taste! 🫠

Actually, I discovered this place last week on Swiggy while looking for homely food at reasonable prices  something that rarely happens on food apps. But this time, I was lucky! I ordered their thali on Swiggy, and when the parcel arrived, I was pleasantly surprised to see so many delicious dishes packed together. That was the first time I tasted their food.

Today, while returning home, I decided to visit their premises and what a pleasant surprise! Polite service, tempting South Indian dishes, from tangy tomato curry to sweet rice kheer simply divine! 😋 Only in 100 Rs serving on banana leaf

Highly recommend

featured_reviews.name: Gokulraj
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jeevan Boarding House in Chembur is a great spot if you're looking for delicious South Indian meals on a budget!

The ambiance is simple but pleasant, and the food is absolutely worth it.

It’s conveniently located—just a 1-minute walk from Chembur station—making it super easy to reach.

Their meals (Thali) are priced at just ₹90, which is a steal for the quality and quantity you get. Everything served beyond the basic meal is charged extra, but still very affordable.

Meals are served traditionally on a banana leaf, which adds to the authentic experience. The taste is amazing—especially their pineapple sweet and payasam, which are both top notch. You definitely won’t leave hungry, as the portions are more than enough!

Be prepared to wait if you visit during peak hoursit gets quite crowded after 1 PM, but the food is worth the wait. 😄

Highly recommended for anyone craving wholesome South Indian food!

featured_reviews.name: jishnu K V
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited Kerala Cafe today, and unfortunately, it was a very disappointing experience. The place markets itself as serving authentic Kerala cuisine, but the food did not meet our expectations at all.
The prices are extremely high compared to the quantity served. The portion sizes are very small — even the starters are not sufficient for one person. For the amount charged, we expected much better quality and quantity.
We ordered Thalassery Chicken Biryani, but what was served did not resemble authentic Thalassery biryani. Instead of the traditional preparation, it felt like yellow-colored rice with very small, fried-rice-sized chicken pieces. The taste and presentation were nowhere close to what one would expect from a genuine Kerala-style biryani.
We also ordered Pineapple Coconut Salad, but it was served raw and poorly prepared. There were hardly any visible coconut pieces in the dish, which was surprising given the name of the item.
Overall, the experience did not justify the pricing, and the food quality did not match the claims. Except for the Bisleri water, nothing here was satisfactory. I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone specifically looking for authentic Kerala cuisine

I went there after confirming on call with the restaurant that the item is available but I guess the staff were unaware as all of them were non-malayalees.
-The washing area is inside the toilet?

featured_reviews.review_text:
Customer Service:
Extremely disappointing. The staff seemed in a rush to close and showed little interest in attending to customers. The attitude was unprofessional and far from acceptable for a dining establishment.
Food Quality:
We ordered two different chicken dishes expecting distinct flavors, as described on the menu. Unfortunately, both tasted very similar, as if the chicken had been pre-boiled and simply mixed into different gravies. This was quite underwhelming.
Food Quantity:
For a price of around ₹400 per dish, the portion size did not justify the cost. It felt overpriced for what was served.
Hidden Charges:
A 10% “voluntary” tip was added to the bill without prior consent. Given the poor service experience, this felt unreasonable and inappropriate.
Overall Experience:
This is a genuine review based on my experience visiting multiple restaurants in and around Mumbai. This was by far one of the worst experiences I’ve had, and unfortunately, I would not consider returning.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I request Google to give me option of giving zero stars! I have never had worse biryani than this i swear.. and i am pretty sure now that the management team is not from kerala neither their chef is a keralite! I request the owner to have a Thalassery biryani from any near by good restaurant and know how it tastes like! Have it from any road side shop also it will taste better than yours! I ordered Thalassery chicken biryani and prawns biryani.. if you are ordering the chicken biryani for your dog you may proceed with it because they give small 4 chicken bone only.. with hardly 1cm of meat attached with it.. the chicken parts you buy for your dog have 10 times more chicken meat than the amount you get in their chicken biryani! With some pathetic yellow rice which you will feel like giving out flavours like a spoiled biryani! Prawns biryani masala was edible compared to the chicken biryani.. but then it will have chunks of some ration rice kind of plain white rice with no salt even forget about masala.. it will turn to your worst nightmare in biryani guys.. trust me.. for the first time in life had to throw away the papadam because it was fried in tar oil i think.. I never thought people could attain such talents in cooking to spoil the papadam.. worst experience ever..
I have no idea what you are charging for.. is it for the ration rice used for making biryani, bone of chicken, or tar oil used for frying papadam or maybe even for the amount of water added in the curd with some free floating onions in it..

If you are thinking of having biryani from here trust me guys take a cooker put some rice in it and however you cook the rice it will taste better than their biryani rice.. and get some curd add 10 times water in it mix and have it.. it will taste better.. even they give the similar curd and rice! Thank me later for this advice..

Team Kerala cafe please remove biryani from your menu.. it is a sin to make people eat biryani which taste like this.. biryani is an emotion to many and you guys are creating mental trauma.. and for God sake order a Thalassery biryani and have it from somewhere else or just see some pictures from YouTube or Google!

featured_reviews.name: Pradeep Ramakrishnan
featured_reviews.review_text:
"In a land of blind men, a one eyed man is King."

This perfectly exemplifies Anna Idli, a medium-sized eatery at Fort, Mumbai. Darling of the influencers, a bevy of testimonials hits you at the entrance. The ambience is cool, comforting and welcoming. The service is passable - no complaints on that front. But when it comes to the main reason why people go to a restaurant - the food - Anna Idli fails miserably. The sambhar has more sugar than a pack of sugar boiled toffees. The chutneys are cold, uninviting. The Dosa has so much oil that you wonder if it was dipped in oil and fried.

Anna Idli is evidence that outside Mani's in Chembur and the basket idli-wallahs in Fort /Nariman Point, there's very little South Indian tiffin that can really pass the taste and authenticity test.

Well, for the price, when I am not even recommending the food, does it matter?

Feedback Regarding Hygiene Practices at the Shop

I usually support small, hardworking local shops and understand that space may be limited. However, hygiene must always be a priority, especially when handling food.

Today, during my visit in the morning, I noticed something very concerning. The person preparing the chutney dropped some of it on the dirty floor while transferring it from one vessel to another — and instead of discarding it, he picked it up and put it back into the container. He was also using dirty water and mixing it with his bare, unwashed hands.

This kind of practice is dangerous and could harm customers' health. I hope the shop takes this feedback seriously and improves their hygiene standards going forward.

Visited Anna Idli Centre expecting authentic South Indian taste, but it was a complete disappointment. The idlis were stale, the sambhar was bland and watery, and the chutneys tasted like they had been sitting out for hours.

The place has no seating arrangements, forcing customers to stand in a dirty environment. The hygiene was appalling, with filthy floors and unclean serving areas.

To top it off, the shop owner was rude and arrogant, and dishonest refusing to address any complaints and behaving as if they didn’t care about their customers at all.

If you value good food, cleanliness, and basic decency, avoid this place at all costs. It’s the worst experience I’ve ever had!
